items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: one of them being Joe Williams. I did a thing, I was back in California again with him. We were there for something like two or three weeks. After that we did a club in Chicago

ctx.x: a group. Down the street in the Sherman Hotel was Cab Calloway's band. Duke Ellington was playing the Stephens Hotel. There was just music everywhere, with all kinds of names. And between shows, we'd just go around and meet all these people. And I got to know so many musicians who became lifetime friends, who ended up being friends.

Then, the fact is that Chicago at that particular time, like all other cities, had its sections where the Blacks lived and congregated. Now, this was all downtown in what they call the Loop in Chicago. But afterwards, everybody went out to the South Side, White and Black, and that's when they had clubs out there like the... They had a club called the Rhumboogie where Coleman Hawkins was playing. There was a club where Joe Williams used to work, one of the most popular... I can't remember now. I'll think of it…

This is actually where I really met my very good and lifetime friend, Al Hibbler, the singer. Since then we've had many associations. I really met him out there, and he and I became very fast friends. It was just an enjoyable time.
